title: Degrees, Radians and Reference Angles
seo_title: Precalculus Degrees, Radians and Reference Angles Worksheets (TEKS P.4B, P.4C)
standard_text: P.4B describe the relationship between degree and radian measure on the unit circle; P.4C represent angles in radians or degrees based on the concept of rotation and find the measure of reference angles and angles in standard position
meta_desc: Free Precalculus worksheets for Texas TEKS P.4B and P.4C: convert degrees and radians, coterminal and reference angles, standard position and angles of rotation. 100 questions with answers.
key_sub: Coterminal angles differ by full turns of 2π.
body_html:
How to think about it

  • A full turn is 360° = 2π radians, so 180° = π radians.
  • Degrees to radians: multiply by π180. Radians to degrees: multiply by 180π.
  • An angle in standard position starts on the positive x-axis. Counterclockwise is positive.
  • Coterminal angles differ by full turns. The reference angle is the acute angle to the x-axis.

Examples

Example

Convert 135°

135 × π180

Answer: 3π4

Example

Reference angle of 7π6

210°, Quadrant III

210° − 180°

Answer: π6

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Using 180/π to get radiansDegrees to radians uses π/180.
Measuring from the y-axisReference angles go to the x-axis.
A full turn of πA full turn is 2π.
